question: M40 section 6(iv): does TMD-proximitised magic-angle graphene, with the Biswas-Sensarma-Randeria nodal-candidate order parameter, have odd Chern parity (-1)^nu at the vortex level -- i.e. can 'nodal MATBG' and 'vortex Majorana' still be true together via induced Ising SOC?  (Sato-Fujimoto arXiv:1007.4369: parity odd => stable vortex Majorana even in a gapless nodal SC.)

MODEL_CHOICES.normal_state: single spin-degenerate band, square-lattice tight binding xi(k) = -2t(cos kx + cos ky) - mu; minimal C2-compatible regularisation of the IKS spin-degenerate Chern-zero hole pocket at Gamma (M40 6(iii))
MODEL_CHOICES.FLAG_lattice_regularisation: the real system's continuum pocket at Gamma is represented by a lattice band; the TRIM at X, Y, M are regulator artifacts whose normal-state energies (4t-eps, 4t-eps, 8t-eps) are set by the regularisation, not by MATBG.  The parity criterion is TRIM-global, so any conclusion that depends on a pair-breaking field exceeding those artifact energies is a regulator statement, not physics.  Flagged wherever it bites.
MODEL_CHOICES.FLAG_square_vs_C2: the square lattice has C4 > C2; the IKS state has only C2. Nothing in the parity criterion uses C4, and the d-wave form treats X and Y asymmetrically, so no spurious degeneracy is imposed at the TRIM.
MODEL_CHOICES.ising_soc: valley-Zeeman-like: Ising SOC in graphene is VALLEY-ODD, so in a one-valley effective block it is a sigma_z Zeeman-like term +lambda_I; the other valley gets -lambda_I.  The two valley blocks are computed separately and the total vortex-level parity is the PRODUCT of the per-valley parities.
MODEL_CHOICES.FLAG_intra_valley_pairing: each valley block pairs k with -k WITHIN the block (intra-valley pairing).  Real MATBG pairing is inter-valley; for an inter-valley singlet, Ising SOC enters the BdG as an effective spin-dependent chemical-potential shift (both pair members shift together -- this is exactly why Ising superconductors are protected) and is then NOT a parity-flipping field at all.  The per-valley treatment used here is therefore the MOST FAVOURABLE honest reading for the window; the inter-valley reading closes it outright.
MODEL_CHOICES.rashba_arm: lambda_R (sin ky sigma_x - sin kx sigma_y); vanishes at every TRIM, so it cannot move the Pfaffian -- verified numerically (rashba_invariance_check)

order_parameters.d_wave: real singlet Delta(k) = Delta2 (cos kx - cos ky), Delta0 = 0 forced (Biswas et al.); NOTE it does NOT vanish at X, Y (|Delta| = 2 Delta2 there)
order_parameters.triplet_polar: triplet, k-independent d-vector, polar phase d||z: Delta(k) = Delta_p sin kx (sigma_z i sigma_y).  FLAG: the lobe direction (sin kx vs sin ky) is a choice; any odd form vanishes at ALL four TRIM, which is the only property the criterion sees

flat_band_calibration.note: flat-band peculiarity: induced Ising SOC lambda_I up to ~3 meV is NOT small against W = 2.922 meV -- lambda_I/W up to ~1, i.e. lambda_I/t up to ~8

benchmark_2_swave_rashba_zeeman.criterion: odd parity iff h^2 > xi_Gamma^2 + Delta^2 (with all other TRIM factors positive); numeric Pfaffian must equal analytic product

sweep_grid.note_eps: mu = -4t + eps; eps < 4 => Fermi surface encloses Gamma only; eps = 4.5 crosses the X/Y TRIM. eps in meV = eps * t_meV; the honest MATBG pocket E_F ~ 1-3 meV corresponds to eps ~ 2.7-8.2, of which only eps < 4 is a Gamma-only pocket on this lattice -- E_F >~ 1.5 meV cannot be represented as a Gamma-only pocket at all (regulator limitation, flagged)
sweep_grid.note_lambda_I: 0-0.1 is the prescribed conservative grid (7-37 ueV under the flat-band mapping); 1.0, 2.74, 5.48, 8.21 t = 0.37, 1, 2, 3 meV are the flat-band-honest extension, lambda_I/W up to ~1

rashba_invariance_check.meaning: Rashba vanishes at every TRIM; the Pfaffians are exactly lambda_R-independent
Rashba vanishes at every TRIM; the Pfaffians are exactly lambda_R-independent

valley_product_theorem.statement: valley - block = sigma_x (valley + block) sigma_x at every TRIM (Rashba vanishes there; the singlet/triplet gap picks up at most a global sign), so the per-valley parities are equal point-by-point and the total parity = (per-valley parity)^2 = +1 wherever defined.  A single-valley odd result can therefore NEVER survive at the two-valley vortex level in this model unless valley symmetry is broken in the normal state or the pairing is valley-polarised -- which the IKS spin-degenerate normal state and the Biswas classification both exclude.

verdict.statement: WINDOW CLOSED at the vortex level.  The total (two-valley) Chern parity (-1)^nu is EVEN at every point of the sweep, for both the real d-wave and the polar-triplet order parameter, including the flat-band-honest corner lambda_I ~ W where induced Ising SOC is as large as the entire flat-band width.  The reason is structural, not numerical: Ising SOC is valley-odd, the two valley blocks are spin-rotation images of each other at every TRIM, their parities are equal point-by-point, and the vortex-level parity is their product -- a perfect square.  PER-VALLEY parity DOES go odd at honest parameters (lambda_I > E_F on the Gamma pocket, e.g. lambda_I ~ 1 meV against E_F ~ 1 meV, both well within measured induced-SOC and flat-band scales), so the Sato-Fujimoto mechanism is genuinely activated by Ising SOC within a single valley -- and then exactly doubled and cancelled by the other valley.  Nodal MATBG plus induced Ising SOC does NOT yield a vortex Majorana in this minimal model.  What WOULD reopen it: valley polarisation of the normal state or of the pairing (excluded at nu = -2 by the IKS evidence and by Biswas et al.), or genuine Rashba admixture large enough to matter -- which is what M40 6(i) already closed.
verdict.sharpest_caveat: the closure rests on the valley-product structure of a model in which each valley pairs with itself.  Real MATBG pairing is inter-valley: there Ising SOC is not even pair-breaking (it shifts both members of a time-reversed inter-valley pair together), which closes the window MORE decisively, not less.  But both statements are made on a one-pocket square-lattice regularisation of an IKS normal state that has never been treated in the BM continuum model with proximitised SOC; a real BM-model Pfaffian calculation remains the only way to make this closure (or any reopening) load-bearing.

HONESTY: (i) this is a one-pocket square-lattice regularisation, not the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model; three of the four TRIM are regulator artifacts, and results that depend on pair-breaking fields reaching the artifact TRIM energies (lambda_I >= ~4t-eps) are regulator statements
(ii) the valley-product subtlety is not a caveat here, it is the result: it kills every single-valley odd-parity conclusion (computed, not assumed -- see valley_product_theorem)
(iii) a positive (odd) result -- which did not occur at the total level -- would have been an invitation to a real BM-model calculation, not a device claim; the same standard applies to this closure

(iv) all conclusions are conditional on the Biswas-Sensarma-Randeria order-parameter classification (real singlet d with Delta0 = 0, or triplet p with k-independent d-vector, no admixture) from the IKS normal state
(v) intra-valley pairing was used per valley block; inter-valley pairing (the physical case) makes Ising SOC non-pair-breaking and closes the window independently
(vi) E_F ~ 2-3 meV of the measured flat band cannot be represented as a Gamma-only pocket on this lattice (saddle at 1.46 meV under the calibration); the eps < 4t rows are the trustworthy ones
